entities.label: Open Inventor
entities.blurb: SGI's C++ scene-graph toolkit whose ASCII file format became the literal DNA of VRML 1.0.

entities.label: VRML 1.0

milestones.what: conceived around the WWW94 conference and www-vrml list

entities.blurb: The first attempt at a 3D web: static hyperlinked worlds described in a dialect of Open Inventor.

entities.label: VRML 2.0 / VRML97

milestones.what: SGI's Moving Worlds wins the VRML 2.0 RFP

entities.blurb: Animated, scriptable virtual worlds standardized after a six-proposal shootout that SGI's Moving Worlds won over Microsoft's ActiveVRML.

entities.label: ActiveVRML

milestones.what: lost VRML 2.0 vote; evolved into DirectAnimation/Chromeffects

entities.blurb: Microsoft's reactive, functional-programming rival bid for the VRML 2.0 crown, elegant but rejected by the community vote.

entities.label: X3D
entities.blurb: VRML's XML-clad successor that kept the ISO torch of the open 3D web burning long after the plugins died.

entities.label: Wavefront OBJ
entities.blurb: Wavefront Technologies' plain-text mesh format that outlived its creator to become 3D's lowest common denominator.

entities.label: STL
entities.blurb: 3D Systems' bare-triangles stereolithography format from 1987 that still feeds nearly every 3D printer on Earth.

entities.label: PLY
entities.blurb: Stanford's polygon format, designed by Greg Turk to store scanned geometry like the famous Stanford Bunny.

entities.label: FBX

milestones.what: lands at Autodesk via the Alias acquisition

entities.blurb: Kaydara FiLMBOX's native format that rode two acquisitions to become Autodesk's proprietary lingua franca of game and film pipelines.

entities.label: COLLADA
entities.blurb: Sony's open XML interchange schema for digital assets, handed to Khronos to fight FBX with openness.

entities.label: glTF
entities.blurb: Khronos's 'JPEG of 3D', a compact runtime delivery format that finally made 3D assets load like images on the web.

entities.label: USD (Universal Scene Description)

milestones.what: USDZ unveiled with Apple at WWDC
AOUSD alliance formed to standardize it

entities.blurb: Pixar's open-sourced film pipeline scene format, now courted by Apple, NVIDIA, and Adobe as the metaverse's authoring backbone.

entities.label: VRM
entities.blurb: Japan's glTF-based humanoid avatar format that lets VTubers carry one body across any app that speaks it.

entities.label: OpenXR
entities.blurb: Khronos's royalty-free API that ended the VR runtime format wars by letting one binary target every headset.

entities.label: Web3D Consortium
entities.blurb: The nonprofit that shepherded VRML into ISO and has kept an open, royalty-free 3D web standard alive ever since.

entities.label: Khronos Group
entities.blurb: The industry consortium behind OpenGL, Vulkan, COLLADA, glTF, and OpenXR — the standards engine room of real-time 3D.

entities.label: Metaverse Standards Forum
entities.blurb: A Khronos-convened coordination body where thousands of companies try to make metaverse standards interoperate instead of collide.

entities.label: Alliance for OpenUSD
entities.blurb: Pixar, Adobe, Apple, Autodesk, and NVIDIA's Linux Foundation alliance to turn USD into a formal open standard.

entities.label: Labyrinth
entities.blurb: Mark Pesce and Tony Parisi's scrappy 1994 prototype 3D web browser whose WWW94 demo willed VRML into existence.

entities.label: WebSpace Navigator
entities.blurb: SGI and Template Graphics' Inventor-powered viewer, the first commercial VRML browser the world could actually run.

entities.label: WorldView

milestones.what: licensed to Microsoft for Internet Explorer

entities.blurb: Intervista's WorldView put VRML on ordinary Windows PCs and rode Internet Explorer to tens of millions of desktops.

entities.label: Live3D
entities.blurb: Paper Software's WebFX reborn as Netscape Live3D, the VRML plugin bundled straight into Navigator at the browser war's peak.

entities.label: Cosmo Player

milestones.what: sold with Cosmo Software to Platinum Technology, then CA

entities.blurb: SGI's polished VRML97 player, the de facto reference browser of the VRML era until corporate hand-offs orphaned it.

entities.label: Community Place
entities.blurb: Sony CSL's multi-user VRML 2.0 browser and server, filling shared worlds with avatars years before 'metaverse' was a pitch deck.

entities.label: blaxxun Contact
entities.blurb: Black Sun/blaxxun's avatar-filled VRML community client, named straight out of Snow Crash's Black Sun bar.

entities.label: Cortona3D
entities.blurb: ParallelGraphics' Cortona plugin quietly inherited the VRML userbase after Cosmo's demise and pivoted into industrial 3D documentation.

entities.label: FreeWRL
entities.blurb: The long-running open-source VRML/X3D browser that kept the standard runnable when the commercial players vanished.

entities.label: X3DOM
entities.blurb: Fraunhofer IGD's framework that dropped X3D scenes straight into the HTML DOM via WebGL — declarative 3D with no plugin at all.

entities.label: Vivaty (Media Machines / Flux)
entities.blurb: Tony Parisi's X3D-powered Flux player grown into Vivaty's in-browser virtual worlds, whose assets Microsoft picked up at shutdown.

entities.label: Unity Web Player

milestones.what: deprecated as browsers dropped NPAPI plugins

entities.blurb: The plugin that made real game engines routine inside browsers — until the plugin era itself was abolished.

entities.label: three.js
entities.blurb: Ricardo Cabello's WebGL library that became the default substrate for practically all post-plugin 3D on the web.

entities.label: A-Frame
entities.blurb: Mozilla's HTML-tag framework for WebVR that let anyone author a virtual world in a page of markup — VRML's spirit, reborn on three.js.

entities.label: Sketchfab
entities.blurb: The YouTube of 3D models, which normalized embedding interactive 3D in any web page.

entities.label: FireBox
entities.blurb: James McCrae's 2014 experiment that treated web pages as rooms and hyperlinks as portals — the seed that became JanusVR.

entities.label: JanusVR

milestones.what: company founded by McCrae and Singh in December
company folds; code released as open source

entities.blurb: The VR internet browser where webpages are rooms and links are portals, built by a Toronto team who open-sourced it all on the way out.

entities.label: JanusWeb
entities.blurb: James Baicoianu's three.js-based engine that brought JanusVR's portal-linked rooms to any plain web browser, no install required.

entities.label: JanusXR
entities.blurb: The community continuation of the Janus vision — an immersive, decentralized web of collaborative 3D spaces, kept alive by its ex-JanusVR builders.

entities.label: Elation Engine
entities.blurb: Baicoianu's modular JavaScript game engine, the quiet foundation under JanusWeb's virtual worlds.

entities.label: Silicon Graphics (SGI)
entities.blurb: The graphics-workstation titan whose Inventor toolkit, Moving Worlds spec, and Cosmo browser defined the first 3D web.

entities.label: Netscape
entities.blurb: The browser company that bought its way into VRML by swallowing Paper Software and shipping Live3D to the masses.

entities.label: Sony
entities.blurb: Twice-pivotal in open 3D: co-author of Moving Worlds and Community Place in the 90s, birthplace of COLLADA in the 2000s.

entities.label: Microsoft
entities.blurb: Lost the VRML 2.0 spec war with ActiveVRML, then simply licensed Intervista's WorldView to put VRML in Internet Explorer anyway.

entities.label: Apple
entities.blurb: Pitched 'Out of This World' in the VRML 2.0 contest, then returned decades later to champion USDZ and co-found AOUSD.

entities.label: Pixar
entities.blurb: The animation studio that gave its production scene format, USD, to the world and reshaped 3D interchange.

entities.label: Autodesk
entities.blurb: The design-software giant whose acquisition chain made FBX the proprietary toll bridge of 3D pipelines.

entities.label: Kaydara
entities.blurb: The Montreal motion-capture house whose FiLMBOX product left behind a file format far more famous than itself: FBX.

entities.label: Alias Systems
entities.blurb: Maya's maker, the middle link that carried FBX from Kaydara into Autodesk's empire.

entities.label: Intervista Software
entities.blurb: Tony Parisi's VRML startup, whose WorldView browser was the format's beachhead on the Windows desktop.

entities.label: Paper Software
entities.blurb: The tiny upstate-New York shop whose WebFX plugin was good enough that Netscape bought the whole company.

entities.label: blaxxun interactive
entities.blurb: The Snow Crash-named Munich/SF company that ran some of the largest avatar communities of the VRML age.

entities.label: Mozilla
entities.blurb: Firefox's steward, whose MozVR team seeded the WebVR API era and gave the world A-Frame.

entities.label: Unity Technologies
entities.blurb: The engine democratizer whose Web Player era and later hiring of Tony Parisi tied it into web 3D's long arc.

entities.label: Mark Pesce
entities.blurb: The evangelist-engineer who co-created Labyrinth and willed a 'VRML' community into existence with a mailing list and a vision.

entities.label: Tony Parisi
entities.blurb: Web 3D's ultimate recurring character: Labyrinth, WorldView, Flux/Vivaty, and glTF all bear his fingerprints across three decades.

entities.label: Gavin Bell
entities.blurb: The SGI engineer who translated Open Inventor into the VRML 1.0 spec and co-edited VRML 2.0.

entities.label: Rikk Carey
entities.blurb: Co-editor of the VRML 2.0/97 specification at SGI and co-author of the Annotated VRML reference.

entities.label: Neil Trevett
entities.blurb: Khronos's long-serving president, the standards diplomat behind glTF, OpenXR, and the Metaverse Standards Forum.

entities.label: James McCrae
entities.blurb: The Toronto graphics researcher who built FireBox, co-founded JanusVR, and still keeps the native client alive as JanusXR.

entities.label: James Baicoianu
entities.blurb: Builder of the Elation Engine and JanusWeb, who carried the Janus vision onto the open web and into its community era.

entities.label: Karan Singh
entities.blurb: University of Toronto graphics professor who co-founded JanusVR with his former student James McCrae.

entities.label: Fabrice Robinet
entities.blurb: The engineer at the origin of glTF, who led its creation inside the Khronos COLLADA working group.
